about.title: Pleasant Hill Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Pleasant Hill's collision counts reflect a city built around busy connector roads — Contra Costa Boulevard, Taylor Boulevard, Monument Boulevard, and the I-680 interchange all see regular traffic. Contra Costa County's public records show 144 injury collisions and 194 injured people in the most recent final year, with Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. showing up often. Behind those numbers are real people dealing with medical bills, missed work, and insurance calls they didn't ask for. LawProactive isn't a law firm — we're a free service that connects you with an independent personal injury attorney working on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover. Before you talk to any insurance adjuster, it helps to have someone looking out for your side of the story. We can help you get that conversation started quickly, without any obligation.

whyChoose.title: What to Know Before You Move Forward

items.title: Your Clock Is Already Running
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the crash date to file a personal injury claim, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity (like a city or county road agency) was involved. Acting early protects your options.

items.title: Fault Doesn't Have to Be All-or-Nothing
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you're found partly responsible for the collision, you may still recover a reduced share of damages. An independent attorney can help make sure blame isn't unfairly pinned on you.

items.title: Skip the Recorded Statement
items.desc: The other driver's insurer may ask for a recorded statement soon after the crash — you're not required to give one. Speaking with an attorney first helps preserve evidence and keeps your words from being used against you later.

items.question: How long do I have to file a car accident claim in Pleasant Hill?
items.answer: Under California law, you generally have two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. If a government entity, like a city road department, contributed to the crash, that deadline can shrink to as little as six months. Talking to an attorney early helps make sure you don't miss a critical deadline.

items.question: Why do so many crashes happen around Contra Costa Boulevard and the I-680 area?
items.answer: Public collision records show these corridors carry heavy commuter and local traffic, and Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. tend to show more reported crashes. These are simply patterns in the public data, not a judgment about any specific road or intersection. Regardless of where it happened, the legal steps after a crash are similar.

items.question: Should I speak with the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: You're not obligated to give a recorded statement to the other insurer, and doing so before speaking with an attorney can sometimes work against you. Insurance adjusters often ask questions designed to minimize your claim. It's usually best to let an attorney handle those conversations on your behalf.
